source_text: Non ergo invidemus Salvatorem illi, quam Conditoris sui dignitate defendimus; sed malum eam negamus esse, ne efficiamur Manichaei, malum ei negamus inesse, ne mutatis nominibus simus totidem Manichaei.
pass_a_gloss: We therefore do not begrudge a Savior to that which we defend by the dignity of its Founder; but we deny it is evil, lest we be made Manichaeans; we deny evil is in it, lest with names changed we be the same number of Manichaeans.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: We therefore do not begrudge a Savior to the nature we defend on the grounds of its Creator’s dignity. We deny that it is evil, so as not to become Manichaeans; we deny that evil is in it, so as not to be the very same Manichaeans under changed names.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
